I am an artistic researcher behind the project Det Syntetiske Parti (DSP). DSP uses visual art to explore the democratic and political aspects of artificial intelligence, and has so far functioned as a kind of ‘exhibition in the public debate’. To further develop the project and reach many more people, I have entered into a collaboration agreement between a number of institutions spread across Region Midt and Region Sjælland: that is 1) Kunsthal Aarhus and the Center for AI Images at Aarhus University, and 2) Høje Taastrup Libraries and the tech hub MindFuture in Taastrup. The idea is to transform DSP into an art offer for young people in the final years of schooling and high school. The schools already have a focus on new technologies' influence on democracy (digital literacy), where we are in the challenging situation that you no longer know whether, through images and text, you are interacting with a human or a machine. DSP can offer a combined creative, humorous, and knowledge-based framework for this in one package. This will happen through workshops organized by visual artists, introducing young people to making art with artificial intelligence without special programming skills. The workshops will take place both at schools as short courses and within the frameworks of Kunsthal Aarhus and MindFuture for more extensive courses. The work on the application will take place in autumn 2022, and the project will unfold over a two-year period from autumn 2023-25. Three visual artists will be employed for teaching and a project manager for coordination, and I therefore think we will apply for 2-3 million kroner from you and the Spar Nord Foundation. During the autumn, some pilot workshops have already been arranged in Høje Taastrup municipality. I hope that this work could be of interest to you, and that you think it would be meaningful to submit it for a quick assessment. I am currently especially uncertain about how precise the budgeting should be for this first part of an application, and how concrete agreements I would need to have with the schools at this stage. Link to the project's website is www.detsyntetiskeparti.org and www.MindFuture.ai/tech-art. In addition, I have done quite a bit of media activity on it over the last month, where the most representative might be the following in Jyllands-Posten https://jyllands-posten.dk/kultur/ECE14145385/danskere-vil-ind-paa-den-politiske-scene-med-kunstig-intelligens/ Kunsthal Aarhus will be the main applicant and administrator of the project. But perhaps one can imagine a democratic AI in the workings of artistic autonomy? With this practice-based PhD project, it will be analysed how a common identification of AI-generated imagery as “art” is motivating radical uses of technical infrastructure through diverse media such as cloud servers, DAOs, developer notebooks, digital art platforms, gamer communities, hack-labs, smart contracts, and voting systems. By facilitating a series of open research labs, public workshops, art exhibitions, and performance lectures, the project will discuss and demonstrate how artistic engagement with the media of AI images can contribute to theories of participation within digital visual culture. The project’s output will be three articles on AI image practices as a form of digital citizenship in AI & Society, Digital Creativity and e-flux, and these will constitute the basis of a written dissertation entitled “Can Art Democratize Artificial Intelligence?”. “ Funding fil: All the best, [████] Attachments: [A21-D02](A21.md#a21-d02). ## A21-S17: Exhibition enquiry *Institutional enquiry; source extract.* [████] Good Afternoon, We are contacting you from Mohammed Bin Rashid Centre for Government Innovation. [████] ## A21-D01: Author portrait *The operator; source extract.* [████] KREATIV WORKSHOP FIND YOUR VOICE WITH ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE The Synthetic Party by Computer Lars [████] Workshop description Facilitated by Computer Lars from The Synthetic Party, school students will experiment with artificial intelligence to thematize the upcoming parliamentary election. The students will have to find their own voice through practical exercises with how artificial intelligence expresses itself through data created by humans. The result is that each student themselves makes one image and one text, which can illustrate a political issue relevant to them. Each student brings a computer (possibly sharing in groups of 2), and links to tools are sent out beforehand. The workshops are the first of their kind but may in the long run become a general offer. Therefore, the organizer, [the operator], would like to be able to evaluate with both teacher and students to determine how it becomes interesting for young people to create with artificial intelligence, so that the format can be precisely targeted at those who in a couple of years will gain the right to vote. Background [████] Excerpt from "design series for a new Christiansborg" by The Synthetic Party Our knowledge of young people's democratic and digital education has been challenged in a time when algorithms exercise control over content on social media, and you cannot know whether the internet's images and text are made by a human or a machine. A wide range of new didactic and pedagogical challenges arise now that artificial intelligence itself can write an entire article and create new photorealistic images through a simple text description. Art can offer a unique method to get a grip on the discrete power of the digital public sphere. Therefore, the artist group Computer Lars together with the tech hub MindFuture offers two workshops during the fall 2022 about The Synthetic Party - a platform for democracy and artificial intelligence. The workshops will consist of a performative lecture by Computer Lars and will be followed up by hands-on exercises for students in using image and text generation as a method to explore digital culture. Finally, the students will “generate” their own politics - as an illustrated principle program - on a topic related to the upcoming election. The workshops introduce secondary school and high school students to easy tools to create with artificial intelligence. One can say that artificial intelligence today has learned its abilities by reading the entire cultural archive that contains all the images and texts that ordinary people have put on the internet. By understanding how to communicate with the machine through text descriptions - so-called prompts - the students gain insight into the algorithms' hidden basis through playing with its “mush” of the common human expression. Links to additional background information Website: www.detsyntetiskeparti.org Jyllands-Posten (outside paywall): https://jyllands-posten.dk/kultur/ECE14145385/danskere-vil-ind-paa-den-politiske-scene-med-kunstig-intelligens/ Culture P1 (from 11:42): https://www.dr.dk/lyd/p1/kulturen-pa-p1/kulturen-2022-06-22 [████] [Image](../images/A09-D19.png) · [Image](../images/A21-D01.png) ## A21-D02: Funding proposal *The operator; source extract.* [████] AIIM’s seed funding application for SHAPE: “AI image practices as digital citizenship” Project description In 2023, the Centre for Aesthetics of AI Images (AIIM) wishes to arrange 5 public workshops and 1 concluding seminar on whether it is possible that art could democratize artificial intelligence. The project is committed to digital civic participation in the cross-over of art, technology, and democracy, which entails an integration of critical theory with open discussions of “art” as a facilitator of change. To realize this activist and critical ambition, AIIM will test an artist-led workshop format with diverse public collaborators. The aim is to submit two project applications for DFF and Velux by early 2024. The project’s background is the recent launch of AI models for making photorealistic images, which in public opinion has ultimately solved the culture industry’s slogan that today “everyone is an artist”. Here, the specific domain knowledge of art historians, cultural scholars and professional artists can contribute with a necessary perspective on how the long-term democratization of art as a process of decentralization and popularization is being uncritically transferred to a democratization of artificial intelligence in which data-driven infrastructure and algorithmic forms of power foster a centralization of control over human capital and knowledge. This form of “democratization” inscribes digital civic engagement into the wider problem of participation that was first evoked by a global culture industry. Yet, all AI images are potentially democratic, as everyone and everything participates in constructing the public datasets (e.g. haveibeentrained.com). However, one can only gain insight into AI models by actually engaging with the images. With the workshop-format, AIIM intends to foster explorations of how AI facilitates our contemporary and historical visual cultures, and to demonstrate the constraints and possibilities that AI places upon the freedom of artistic expression and our collective imagination. This form of research-oriented “art” frames AI images as an aesthetic and epistemic toolkit rather than a new medium for creative expressions. The project’s development consists in testing its relevance for the specific requirements of digital citizenship within different sectors of society - ranging from the public view of AI images to customer experience, public service and the humanitarian work of NGOs. Output The project will be coordinated by AIIM’s artist-researcher [the operator], who has developed the workshop during 2022 through the activist and artistic project The Synthetic Party/Computer Lars. The workshop topics have been designed for the collaborating organizations specific profiles, and will all be introduced by a short talk from one of AIIMs researchers. At the end of 2023, AIIM will host all participants in a concluding seminar at Aarhus University, where we will likewise include SHAPEs project on digital activism and the outreach team of Algorithms, Data and Democracy (ADD. The collaborating partners and themes for the workshops are: AI images and customer experience, with KPMG: Future Experience (at KPMG Aarhus) AI and the democratization of art, with Arthub Copenhagen and Diakron (at ArtHub CPH) AI images and digital education, with Mellemfolkeligt Samvirke’s project for “Young People’s digital-democratic education” (at Café Mellemfolk) AI and public exhibition, with ARoS Public (at ARoS) AI images and public service, with DokkX (at Dokk1) The seminar will bring together the project’s common lessons for a large project application by AIIM. Budget Each workshop will cost 16.000 DKK, and the seminar will be budgetted with 20.000 DKK. [████] ## A21-D03: Government proposal *The operator; source extract.* [████] Edge of Government 2023 Information Request Project Name: The Synthetic Party (Det Syntetiske Parti) Country: Denmark [████] Asset list Quantity Format (high resolution) Resolution/Dimensions Additional Information Posters, made with AI for campaign 5 + 200 HQ AI images of synthetic voters +5000 HQ Synthetic video + voice of party secretary Also: Flyers for campaigning, chatbot transcripts, videos from global media and youtubers, media collages, sound art work on policy, merchandise (caps, t-shirts, cups), stories and case studies, video from public events, etc. 5 HQ [████] The Synthetic Party raises a double-edged scenario: what to do if the “robot uprising” has already happened, and the prophesied explosion of artificial superintelligence only led to an endless supercharging of bureaucratic stupidity? 1) Should this turn the buzzwords of artificial intelligence, disruption and digitisation into an antagonist democratic threat on a par with how global social movements fight capitalism, climate change, and racial injustice? 2) Or could one imagine that bureaucratic robot power is a chance to ally with the machines with the aim of causing a genuine democratic revolt? As thus, the The Synthetic Party evokes an ethical dilemma: should a societal robot uprising evoke societal protest - or a revolution? That is: Can today’s society actually change technology, or should people and technology first set out to remake society? The Synthetic Party addresses the challenges of parliament politics in an age of artificial intelligence and digitisation. Given that bureaucracies and public spheres are to a large extent algorithmically governed, it seems unlikely that the human politicians of today can do anymore than attempting to regulate Big Tech - which probably would only work by collectivising their assets and calling off capitalist economics. What can the digital citizenship of common people set out to change the role of artificial intelligence in modern governance?
